rules: Keep model ID, parameter reference, coordinate reference and energy representative attached to every reduced-scale declaration
Convert physical stress and elastic modulus to Pa before forming sigma/E
Convert area and volume using squared and cubed length factors
Preserve per-atom, per-reduced-two-row-cell and per-primitive-interface-cell labels when eV becomes J
Do not equate reduced two-site energy with two full-FCC atomic cells
Keep fixed unit length L0 distinct from candidate equilibrium bPhysical=L0*bStar
Use actual same-candidate area for J/m2 and traction normalization
Missing physical L0 or E0 blocks the associated physical conversion; no default supplied
Do not derive physical temperature, mobility or time from a declared length and energy unit alone
Keep effective axial work volume distinct from independently measured or declared geometric volume
geometryEvidenceRequirements: Specify which object is being determined: bulk atomic primitive volume, interface area, finite probability/collective region, or numerical FVM cell
Same model, parameters, temperature/pressure/reference state, energy counting and boundary conditions
Actual 3D primitive/cell vectors or atom positions with a finite-region partition and explicit length unit
Coordinate-to-jump and collective support mapping, including reference/current strain conventions
Independent geometric area/volume and orientation data, then compare original axial work normalization
Same probability representative, thermal normalization and initial/opening definitions before using finite activation probabilities
nonEquivalences: SI conversion does not establish actual cell geometry
Target reference lattice length is not automatically the actual relaxed candidate length
Saved candidate geometry is not a production material validation
Interface area does not specify a finite collective activation depth
Activation volume, geometric volume, axial effective volume and numerical mesh volume are distinct
A_c is not an energy or geometry conversion factor
